provenance: Official operation and conditional-delete documentation; retained independent Python hashlib/zlib and SigV4 producers. Source/model evidence and local execution do not establish live AWS equivalence.

cases.bounds: 1 through 1000 entries; empty and over-limit whole requests fail before mutation
cases.duplicates: Evaluate separately in original input order; later entries observe prior committed effects
cases.etag: XML supports ordinary bare or quoted validators, normalized to the native quoted entity tag; star denotes existence; weak/list/malformed native validators rejected
cases.authorization: DeleteObject on each entry; a concrete validator additionally requires GetObject; a star alone does not
cases.quiet: Suppress only normal Deleted entries; preserve Error entries and all native interruption positions
cases.integrity: Verify complete bounded XML, terminal framing, and every digest before any entry; accept Content-MD5 or a supported flexible checksum for ordinary SDK defaults
cases.normal: 200 may contain both Deleted and Error; no batch-wide atomicity
cases.unknown: Stop further dispatch; native indexed Unknown aggregate; HTTP whole-request error without a rollback assertion
cases.envelope: 8 MiB decoded XML only for DeleteObjects; other XML retains 64 KiB; both declared and actual lengths are bounded

limitations: AWS conditional-delete documentation does not establish one error code for all missing/concurrent cases. Local missing conditional entries return NoSuchKey; this has not been compared against live AWS.

The DeleteObjects operation page says Content-MD5 is required for general-purpose buckets, while selected modern SDKs use flexible checksums. Local SDK tests accept their supported digest defaults; this broader allowance is not a live AWS observation.
Current missing HTTP bucket privacy follows the shared authority lookup, not a new batch-specific existence disclosure.
